The question is really; Is capitalism functioning as intended when people like Elon Musk have so much control over the markets. The answer is no. You just have to look at what he did to Doge coin to see that he has far more money than is conducive to free markets. He can simply manipulate heaps of important markets because of the amount of money he has. This is a really big problem for capitalism because of how common the problem is in capitalist economies. It's not an argument to say that this is an inherent inevitability or feature of capitalism, because it's antithetical to how capitalism is intended to function. It's like saying that socialism is inherently not very different from fascism, because it always inevitably ends in a Marxist-Leninist dictatorship. Obviously that's not the intention of the system, so the reality of how these systems have panned out isn't a criticism of their design, just the implementation. Socialists are fond of the expression "true socialism has never been tried". But tend not to apply the same standard to capitalism. The question then is, what's the better system by design? Which system is better based off of what it says on the tin? Capitalism has a superior method for managing the economy. In a capitalist system the economy functions autonomously. There are always going to be problems like recessions, price gouging, predatory business practices and exploitation etc, or in socialist economies, black markets, wasteful government misallocation of resources, gradual economic decline and creeping authoritarianism, but on the whole, capitalism gives the economy the ability to autonomously self-correct inefficiencies, and therefore provides superior management of the economy when implemented correctly. Capitalism is also meritocratic. So it goes a long way to addressing Socrates' criticism of democracy leading to demagoguery and lowest common denominator decision making. There's also no need for socialism in order to provide welfare. Welfare can be provided privately in the same way as private health insurance and retirements funds for example, in addition to charities and any number of other strategies. Democracy can work fine when there's no monetary influence allowed on the government. If you remove the government's ability to regulate the economy, there's no advantages to private enterprise in seeking to lobby the government. Also, abolishing donations to political parties goes a long way to preventing collusion between big business and government. If consumers want to change the practices of businesses, they should arrange to boycott those businesses, not hand the responsibility to the government who then inevitably turn around and side with the people who have the most money to offer them. Socialism sounds nice, but so does turning the sea into lemonade. Some things need to be thought through properly before implementation. :OP

My argument against the worry of AI powered humanoid robots taking over and threatening mankind used to be that AI was just another tool, strategy or approach within the programmers toolbox, that among the many tools software developers use to solve or attack various problems, AI is another addition as it has matured over the years. That computers basically sit flat on a desk and all their wiring, circuitry and other components are neatly tucked away within a box. Basically my point is that even a sufficiently advanced AI, no matter how smart, is restricted via the simple and obvious fact that it has no limbs, it’s not mobile, it cannot influence anyone or anything in any physical manner, so how can it be a physical threat? Unless of course WE CHOOSE to design, build, implement and engineer a machine with some sort of physical form, be it modeled directly after human beings or modeled after some other creature or perhaps some new form entirely, the point here is that this machined is endowed, by a group of HUMAN BEINGS, with limbs and physical form that would enable it to be mobile, and THEN proceed to augment it with strong artificial intelligence. So I figured that we would have some sort of AI fairly soon, an impressive AI that begins to show very basic and rudimentary forms of solving problems similar to how human brains approach it but again in very basic and limited ways, however, this AI would still be a software tool sitting inside a box of circuits working in conjunction with other software tools which enable us to solve the next set of problems. To my mind, this is how computers progressed, that the first set of devices were used together to solve problems which helped to make better devices, and when those better devices came along they then helped to solve the problems associated with building even better devices, and so on. And finally, IF the Sci Fi horror vision of humanoid bots taking over were to ever become a reality, that we wouldn’t even see the seeds or beginning of it probably for a long time to come. Yet....here we are, Elon’s company marketing an actual fucking humanoid bot. Of course it won’t be a threat at this stage, but damn this truly is the beginning. PS: I personally think a distinction must be made between Artificial Intelligence and Artificial CONSCIOUSNESS, because it seems like when we ask the question of can a machine be intelligent, or any of the many and varied more detailed and specific questions I’ve heard about this topic, it seems to me their real question and curiosity is whether a machine can be CONSCIOUS or not. I understand intelligence is difficult enough, that a debate about what intelligence even is or how do you measure it can go very deep, and so a detailed and rigorous definition of intelligence would need to be made before anything could be built based upon it. However, while consciousness is equally, if not a way more difficult of a concept to sort of pin down, at least we KNOW what it loosely refers to, that when someone speaks of consciousness even a lay person like me can understand oh ok they are referring to my ability to be self aware, my awareness, admittedly it’s difficult even to describe but I think we know intuitively what it means. And so Artificial Consciousness would obviously refer to a machine that is somehow self aware, that mankind’s dream has finally been realized: we’ve synthesized THOUGHT itself.
